 Massive recall on hot dogs, bacon, deli meat and more: USDA 
 by: Danielle Langenfeld 
 Posted: Oct 19, 2026 / 09:37 AM CDT 
 Updated: Oct 19, 2026 / 10:55 AM CDT 
 by: Danielle Langenfeld 
 Posted: Oct 19, 2026 / 09:37 AM CDT 
 Updated: Oct 19, 2026 / 10:55 AM CDT 
 SHARE 
 ( WJW ) — More than 1.5 million pounds of meat, including hot dogs, bacon, bratwurst, and more, have been recalled, according to the U.S. Department of Agriculture.
 Kayem Foods Inc. is recalling roughly 1,584,361 pounds of its ready-to-eat (RTE) meat and poultry products because they may have been stored at improper temperatures.
 Skin care products tainted with mercury, warns FDA 
 Kayem Foods was first alerted to the potential food-safety issue after receiving a complaint from a retail customer about “warm product temperatures” on Oct. 1, according to a notice published by the USDA’s Food Safety and Inspection Service (FSIS), on Saturday.
 “The establishment investigated and determined that they stored various RTE meat and poultry products in a warehouse cooler that experienced temperature deviations,” the recall notice explained.
 Dozens of products sold under a variety of brand names are impacted. That includes hot dogs, cocktail franks, kielbasa, bratwurst, bacon, brisket, ham steaks, and deli meats such as ham, turkey, bologna, corned beef and liverwurst. A variety of flavored chicken sausage and meatballs have also been recalled.
 According to FSIS, the items were produced between March 31 and Oct. 7 this year, and were shipped to retail and food service locations throughout the U.S. and in Hong Kong.
 A list of product labels shared by the USDA, seen here , shows that items sold under the following brand names are impacted:
 Kayem
 Genoa
 Al Fresco
 Triple M
 McKenzie Country Classics
 Deutschmacher
 Jordan’s
 Essem
 Winnisimmet St. Butchery
 You can find the specific items being recalled on this list from the USDA, which includes the expiration and manufacturing dates of the implicated meat products, as well as their UPC codes and establishment number. More details can be found in the FSIS announcement. 
 So far, there have been no confirmed reports of sickness. However, anyone concerned about an illness is advised to contact a healthcare provider. 
 Consumers are advised to check their refrigerators and freezers. If you purchased any of the products that have since been recalled, you are urged not to eat it. Instead, you are asked to throw it away or return it to the store where you purchased it.
